correctness.rationale: The channel is defined directly by its finite output balls. The nine displayed conflict triples partition all 27 words and each is a clique in the confusability graph, so every correcting code has at most nine words. The nine-word candidate has pairwise disjoint balls. For uniqueness, the finalized verifier reconstructs every ball in two independent ways, exhaustively enumerates every maximal compatibility clique, and independently counts all compatible nine-subsets; both return exactly one maximum, namely the displayed code. The modulo-two lift identity is checked directly.

value.rationale: The parameter is a natural boundary case of the foundational construction: the smallest odd outer alphabet above the binary residue alphabet and the length-three repetition base code. The result is not a mere recomputation of the known construction: it proves an all-code sharp upper bound and complete rigidity. The optimizer has a simple corners-plus-center geometry, and the nine conflict triples give a reusable human-checkable finite certificate for this nonuniform-boundary channel.
